statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: Section 99-19-71(1), read from the enrolled text of 2026 Miss. HB 1546 effective 1 July 2026, provides that any person who has been convicted of a misdemeanor that is not a traffic violation, and who is a first offender, may petition the justice, county, circuit or municipal court in which the conviction was had for an order to expunge the conviction from all public records. Subsection (1) states no waiting period, no completion requirement and no pending-charge restriction; relief is permissive as to petitioning and is treated as discretionary. Under § 99-19-71(3) the Mississippi Criminal Information Center retains a nonpublic record of every expunction solely to determine first-offender status in subsequent proceedings, so an earlier expunction does not restore first-offender status. Section 99-19-72 levies a fee on each petition to expunge an offense under § 99-19-71, collected by the circuit clerk; whether it reaches a subsection (1) petition filed in justice or municipal court is recorded as unresolved.
doNotImport: Do not invent a waiting period, a sentence-completion requirement or a pending-charge bar; subsection (1) contains none.
Do not plead the subsection (2)(a) payment condition as a statutory element of this route; a zero balance is an advisable attachment only.
Do not certify first-offender status or the nontraffic classification; both are the participant's own initialled assertions, checked against the Mississippi criminal history record.
Do not handle a DUI, a traffic violation or a felony on this route; DUI and felonies have their own tracks.
Do not publish a fee amount; § 99-19-72's reach to justice and municipal courts is a recorded open question and the participant confirms the fee with the clerk.
Do not hardcode a court, county, cause number, prosecuting authority, the Greenville address, the three Fourth District counties or the year 2020; every district-variable field is participant data.
Do not reuse the Fourth District models' indictment allegation, race field, five-year recital or attorney-signature phrasing.
Do not extend this family to another Mississippi pathway.

sections.heading: Petition
sections.body: The petitioner, {{participant_full_legal_name}}, petitions this Court, as the court in which the conviction was had, for an order expunging the misdemeanour conviction described below from all public records, pursuant to Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 99-19-71(1), and states:

sections.heading: FIRST. The identifying facts of the conviction
sections.body: FIRST. The identifying facts of the conviction, each taken from the court record:

fieldLabels.charge: Offence of which the petitioner was convicted, worded as the court record words it, with the Mississippi Code section where the record states one
fieldLabels.arresting_agency: Agency that made the arrest or issued the citation
fieldLabels.agency_case_number: That agency's own case or citation number, where the record states one
fieldLabels.disposition_date: Date of the conviction, from the judgment

sections.heading: SECOND.
sections.body: SECOND. The offence is a misdemeanour, and the judgment of this Court is the disposition of the case.

sections.heading: THIRD. The petitioner's own statements
sections.body: THIRD. The following two statements are the petitioner's own, made after the petitioner has reviewed the petitioner's own Mississippi criminal history record. Each is made by the petitioner's initials beside it, and nothing is initialled for the petitioner:

fieldLabels.nontraffic_classification: PETITIONER'S INITIALS The offence is not a traffic violation, and is not a DUI.
fieldLabels.first_offender_status: PETITIONER'S INITIALS I am a first offender. I have no conviction for any other offence, in Mississippi or anywhere else, and I have never had a conviction expunged before.

sections.heading: FOURTH.
sections.body: FOURTH. Section 99-19-71(1) states no waiting period for this petition, and none is asserted or required here.

sections.heading: FIFTH.
sections.body: FIFTH. The petitioner therefore requests that the Court enter an order expunging the conviction described above from all public records, with a nonpublic record retained by the Mississippi Criminal Information Center solely for the purpose Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 99-19-71(3) states.

sections.heading: Declaration
sections.body:
I declare that the facts stated in this petition are true and correct.

(The petitioner signs and dates this petition personally. Nothing on this page is signed or dated for the petitioner.)

documents.title: Exhibit Checklist

sections.heading: EXHIBIT CHECKLIST
sections.body:
Prepared for: {{participant_full_legal_name}}

Attach these exhibits to the petition. Each is named here and obtained by you; nothing is obtained, inspected or authenticated for you.

EXHIBIT A - IN EVERY CASE. A certified copy of the judgment of conviction, from the office that keeps the records of the convicting court. It establishes the court, the offence and the conviction date.

ADVISABLE, AND EXPECTED IN PRACTICE IN MANY COURTS, THOUGH SUBSECTION (1) DOES NOT REQUIRE THEM:

- The docket sheet for the case, from the same office. It shows every court-imposed term and whether each was satisfied.
- An account balance sheet for the case showing a zero balance, from the same office. Subsection (1) does not require payment, but courts commonly require a zero balance in practice.
- Your own Mississippi criminal history record, from the Mississippi Criminal Information Center. It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status across all courts, and self-report is not enough.

Do NOT attach an indictment on this track unless the case was actually indicted; most misdemeanour cases are not, and pleading an indictment that does not exist would be false.

documents.title: Participant Filing Instructions

sections.heading: FILING INSTRUCTIONS
sections.body:
This packet is prepared for expunging a first-offender Mississippi misdemeanour conviction that is not a traffic violation, under Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 99-19-71(1).

Prepared for: {{participant_full_legal_name}}

WHAT YOU DO, IN ORDER

STEP ONE. Identify the correct court and county first. Mississippi has four trial court levels - justice, county, circuit and municipal - that all handle expungements, and people routinely misidentify which one heard their case. The office that keeps the records of the court that entered the conviction can confirm it.

STEP TWO. Ask that office for the case file, the docket sheet, an account balance sheet, and a certified copy of the judgment of conviction. Request your own Mississippi criminal history record from the Mississippi Criminal Information Center, and check the first-offender statement against it before you initial it.

STEP THREE. Call that court's records office before filing and ask whether that court has its own preferred petition or order form or any additional requirement. Mississippi has no statewide form, practice varies by county and circuit district, and this packet defers to the local form wherever one is preferred.

STEP FOUR. Fill in every dotted blank this packet's participant instructions list, from the records. Do not guess a date or a charge wording. Initial the two statements in the petition only if each is true.

STEP FIVE. Sign and date the petition yourself.

STEP SIX. File the petition, with the proposed order and the certificate of service, with the court in which the conviction was had, and pay the filing fee. No fee amount is published in this packet: Miss. Code Ann. Sec. 99-19-72 levies a fee on petitions to expunge an offence under Sec. 99-19-71, but its reach and its collection in lower courts are recorded open questions, so confirm the amount - and any pauper's-affidavit route if you cannot pay - with the court's records office before filing.

STEP SEVEN. Deliver a copy of the petition and the proposed order to the prosecuting authority - for a municipal court case the city prosecutor, not the district attorney - by United States mail or hand delivery, and complete the certificate of service when the copy actually goes out.

STEP EIGHT. Expect that some districts want the district attorney to approve the order as to form before the judicial officer signs. That is a negotiation this packet does not conduct for you.

STEP NINE. After the order issues, obtain certified copies and deliver them to every agency named in the order.

WHAT THE ORDER DOES, FROM THE RECORD

- Fingerprint records are excepted from expungement.
- The Mississippi Criminal Information Center keeps a nonpublic record solely for determining, in subsequent proceedings, whether you are a first offender - so an expunged conviction can still defeat first-offender status later.
- An employer may still ask whether an order of expunction has been entered.

WHEN TO STOP AND GET HELP INSTEAD OF FILING Stop, and take this packet to a lawyer or a legal-aid office, if any of these is true:

- your first-offender status is uncertain, or you have any prior conviction anywhere;
- you have any prior expunged case - an earlier expungement does not restore first-offender status;
- the offence may be a traffic violation - many Mississippi misdemeanours sit close to that line;
- the offence is a DUI, which has its own separate route and is never handled here;
- the conviction is in municipal court and you also have justice court convictions, which may be better handled on the additional-misdemeanours track;
- you are not a United States citizen - expungement does not resolve immigration consequences.

WHAT THIS PACKET DOES NOT TELL YOU

- The filing fee amount, and whether Sec. 99-19-72's fee reaches this petition in this court. The records office of the convicting court is the authority that can answer both.
- Whether your court requires verification or notarization of the petition. No held record establishes a notarization requirement, so the petition carries a simple truth statement; the same office can say whether that court expects more.
- Your court's own preferred forms or local requirements, which vary by county and district. Ask before you file.

WHAT THIS PACKET IS NOT

This is a prepared set of composed pleadings and process pages. Mississippi publishes no statewide expungement form, which is why these pages are composed. It is not legal advice, it is not filed for you, and it does not decide whether the court will grant expungement.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: First-offender status is uncertain, or the participant has any prior conviction anywhere.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: First-offender status is the whole eligibility test on this track and the platform does not certify it; the matter routes to advice.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant has any prior expunged case.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Under § 99-19-71(3) an earlier expungement does not restore first-offender status.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The offence may be a traffic violation.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Subsection (1) excludes traffic violations and many Mississippi misdemeanours sit near that line; the platform does not classify it.
DUI has its own route and is never handled here.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The conviction is in municipal court and the participant also has justice court convictions.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: The matter may be better handled on the additional-misdemeanours track; the packet does not decide it.

hearingAndObjectionStops.situation: The participant is not a United States citizen.
hearingAndObjectionStops.whatItMeans: Immigration consequences are outside the approved self-help boundary.

attachments.title: Certified copy of the judgment of conviction
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court of conviction
attachments.whyNeeded: It establishes the court, the offence and the conviction date, and the conviction date printed in the petition is checked against it.

attachments.title: Mississippi criminal history record
attachments.conditionDescription: Advisable on every track and effectively necessary wherever first-offender status is in issue; the first-offender statement is initialled only after checking it.
attachments.whyNeeded: It is the only reliable way to check first-offender status across all courts; self-report is not enough.

attachments.title: Account balance sheet from the clerk showing a zero balance
attachments.conditionDescription: Advisable everywhere; required in practice in many courts even though subsection (1) does not say so.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court of conviction
attachments.whyNeeded: Courts commonly require a zero balance in practice, and the fines-paid answer is checked against it.

attachments.title: Docket sheet for the case
attachments.conditionDescription: Required in practice on conviction tracks; advisable on every track.
attachments.obtainedFrom: Clerk of the court where the case was heard
attachments.whyNeeded: It shows every court-imposed term and whether each was satisfied.

participantChecklist.text: Identify which of Mississippi's four trial court levels entered the conviction and its county or city, and confirm both with that court's records office.
Obtain the certified judgment, the docket sheet, the account balance sheet and your own Mississippi criminal history record, and fill every blank from the records, never from memory.

Initial the first-offender and nontraffic statements only if each is true after checking the criminal history record; any prior conviction, prior expungement, possible traffic classification or DUI is a stop.
Call the records office of the convicting court before filing to confirm the fee, any pauper's-affidavit route, any preferred local form, the copy count and any approved-as-to-form practice.
Confirm the prosecuting authority and its mailing address with the court's records office, serve by mail or hand delivery, and complete the certificate of service only after service occurs.
